column1: Palindrome Number — given int x, return True if it reads the same backward as forward (negatives are NOT palindromes). Example: 121 → True; -121 → False; 10 → False.
column2: PATTERN: Reverse half the number (avoids string conversion). | INSIGHT: Negative or non-zero ending in 0 → False. Build reversed half until reversed >= remaining; for odd-length numbers, drop the middle digit via rev//10. | STEPS: 1) If x<0 or (x%10==0 and x!=0): False. 2) rev=0; while x>rev: rev=rev*10 + x%10; x//=10. 3) Return x==rev or x==rev//10. | TIME/SPACE: O(log x) / O(1). | PITFALL: The x>rev loop condition handles odd vs even length cleanly.

column1: Plus One — given a digit array (most-significant first) representing a non-negative int, increment by one and return the new digit array. Example: [1,2,3] → [1,2,4]; [9,9] → [1,0,0].
column2: PATTERN: Digit-wise carry propagation from end. | INSIGHT: From the end, +1; if 10, set 0 and carry to next. If everything carries, prepend a 1. | STEPS: 1) For i from n-1 down to 0: if digits[i]<9: digits[i]+=1; return digits. else digits[i]=0. 2) Return [1]+digits. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: All-9s case requires the prepend.

column1: Factorial Trailing Zeroes — given int n, return the number of trailing zeros in n! Example: n=3 → 0 (3!=6); n=5 → 1 (5!=120); n=10 → 2.
column2: PATTERN: Count factors of 5 in n! | INSIGHT: Trailing zeros come from 2·5 pairs; 2s are abundant, so count 5s only. Total = n//5 + n//25 + n//125 + ... (counting multiples, multiples of 25, etc.). | STEPS: 1) count=0. 2) While n: n//=5; count+=n. 3) Return count. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Don't compute n! — way too large/slow.

column1: Sqrt(x) — given non-negative int x, return floor of √x (without using built-in sqrt). Example: 4 → 2; 8 → 2; 0 → 0.
column2: PATTERN: Binary search (or Newton's method). | INSIGHT: Find largest m with m·m ≤ x. | STEPS: 1) If x<2: return x. 2) lo=1, hi=x//2. 3) While lo<=hi: m=(lo+hi)//2; sq=m*m; if sq==x: return m. If sq<x: lo=m+1; else hi=m-1. 4) Return hi. | TIME/SPACE: O(log x) / O(1). | PITFALL: Newton's: r = (r + x/r) / 2 until convergence — also acceptable.

column1: Pow(x, n) — compute x raised to the n-th power (n can be negative). Example: x=2, n=10 → 1024; x=2, n=-2 → 0.25.
column2: PATTERN: Fast exponentiation by squaring. | INSIGHT: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2 for even; x · x^(n-1) for odd. Iterative: walk bits of n. | STEPS: 1) If n<0: x=1/x; n=-n. 2) ans=1. 3) While n: if n&1: ans*=x; x*=x; n>>=1. 4) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Negative n → invert base first.

column1: Max Points on a Line — given a list of 2D points, return the max number of points lying on a single straight line. Example: [[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]] → 3; [[1,1],[3,2],[5,3],[4,1],[2,3],[1,4]] → 4.
column2: PATTERN: For each anchor, hashmap of normalized slopes. | INSIGHT: For each point i, count how many other points share each slope; max + 1 (the anchor) is the best line through point i. Normalize slopes via gcd to avoid float precision. | STEPS: 1) ans=1. 2) For i in range(n): slopes={}. For j!=i: dx=p[j].x-p[i].x; dy=p[j].y-p[i].y; g=gcd(dx,dy) (handle 0); key=(dx//g, dy//g) normalized for sign; slopes[key]+=1. ans=max(ans, max(slopes.values())+1). | TIME/SPACE: O(n²) / O(n). | PITFALL: Float slope is brittle — always normalize via gcd. Handle vertical (dx=0) and duplicate-point cases.
